name: TCST2103 optical endstop module
description: Slotted optical endstop for 3D printers and CNC machines: a Vishay TCST2103 transmissive sensor (IR LED facing an NPN phototransistor across a 3.1 mm slot) with a 180 Ohm LED resistor and a 2.2 kOhm pull-up from S to V, plus an indicator LED. S is LOW while the slot is clear and HIGH while a flag blocks the beam; there is no comparator, so the edge is as slow as the flag. The board is designed for 5 V, so S swings to 5 V and needs a divider on a 3.3 V board. Sold as: TCST2103 optical endstop for RepRap / RAMPS 1.4 (the red 33 x 10 mm board marked End-Stop with a 3-pin JST-XH header printed V S G, usually supplied with a 3-wire cable), e.g. Botland 2659, Hobby Components HC3DPR0015.
eli5: A tiny light gate: a flag on a moving axis slides into its slot, blocks the invisible beam, and the board tells your microcontroller the axis has reached the end.

pins.name: V
pins.description: Supply, 5 V (pin 1, printed V). Feeds the TCST2103 IR LED through 180 Ohm (about 20 mA) and the 2.2 kOhm pull-up on S.

pins.name: S
pins.description: Signal (pin 2, printed S): LOW while the slot is clear, HIGH (pulled to V through 2.2 kOhm) while the beam is blocked. Swings to the 5 V supply, so it reaches a 3.3 V GPIO through a divider.

buildNotes: Header order as printed on the back of the red board: V, S, G. The supplied cable's colours are not standard, so follow the silkscreen, not the wire colour.

Power it from the board's 5V/VBUS pin: the 180 Ohm LED resistor and 2.2 kOhm pull-up are sized for 5 V, and at 3.3 V the LED current drops to about 11 mA, which may not pull S fully low (TCST2103 minimum collector current is 2 mA at IF = 20 mA).

S is pulled up to the 5 V supply, so on an ESP32 or Pico feed it through a divider: 10 kOhm from S to the GPIO and 20 kOhm from the GPIO to GND. A blocked slot then reads about 3.1 V at the pin, a clear slot well under 0.5 V.
S HIGH = triggered (beam blocked). In Marlin this is the usual optical setting (endstop not inverted relative to a normally-closed switch).

There is no comparator or Schmitt trigger: a flag that stops half-way into the beam, or IR-translucent plastic, can leave S at an in-between voltage. Use an opaque flag that passes fully through the slot.
The slot is 3.1 mm wide; the phototransistor switches in about 10 us.

driver.code:
# TCST2103 optical endstop module (red RepRap / RAMPS 1.4 board, header V, S, G),
# MicroPython driver.
# Circuit (board silkscreen R1 = 181, R2 = 222; Jason-B "Improved Optical End-Stop" design):
#   V --180R--> IR LED of the Vishay TCST2103 --> G    (about 20 mA at 5 V)
#   V --2.2k--> S, and the TCST2103 phototransistor pulls S to G while light reaches it.
# So S is:
#   LOW  (0) while the slot is clear (phototransistor on, VCEsat <= 0.4 V)
#   HIGH (1) while a flag blocks the slot (transistor off, 2.2k pulls S to V)
# The board is meant to run from 5 V, so S swings to 5 V: on an ESP32 / Pico put a
# divider on S (e.g. 10k from S to the GPIO, 20k from the GPIO to GND); a logic
# high then reads about 3.1 V at the pin. The phototransistor switches in about
# 10 us (datasheet ton/toff), far faster than any axis.
from machine import Pin
import time


class TCST2103Endstop:
    def __init__(self, pin, debounce_ms=0):
        """pin: GPIO number (or Pin) wired to S (through the divider on a 3.3 V board).
        debounce_ms: optional, require the level to stay the same this long in
        triggered_stable() (useful for a flag that vibrates at the edge of the beam)."""
        self.pin = Pin(pin, Pin.IN) if isinstance(pin, int) else pin
        self.debounce_ms = debounce_ms

    def value(self):
        """Raw level on S: 1 = slot blocked, 0 = clear."""
        return self.pin.value()

    def triggered(self):
        """True while something blocks the slot (S high)."""
        return self.pin.value() == 1

    def triggered_stable(self):
        """Like triggered(), but only returns once S has held one level for debounce_ms."""
        level = self.pin.value()
        start = time.ticks_ms()
        while time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), start) < self.debounce_ms:
            now = self.pin.value()
            if now != level:
                level = now
                start = time.ticks_ms()
        return level == 1

    def irq(self, handler, on_trigger=True):
        """Call handler(pin) when the slot becomes blocked (rising edge) or, with
        on_trigger=False, when it clears again (falling edge)."""
        trig = Pin.IRQ_RISING if on_trigger else Pin.IRQ_FALLING
        return self.pin.irq(handler=handler, trigger=trig)

example.code:
from tcst2103_endstop import TCST2103Endstop
import time

endstop = TCST2103Endstop({S})
while True:
    print('Endstop: %s' % ('TRIGGERED' if endstop.triggered() else 'open'))
    time.sleep_ms(200)

test.title: Reports the endstop triggered when the slot is blocked, open when it clears
